programme.title: Light and Dark
programme.desc: Professor Jim Al-Khalili shows how scientists have used light to reveal almost everything we know about the universe.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: At the turn of the 20th century young sculptors began to be influenced by the `primitive' works of Africa and the Pacific islands, which saw an artistic revolution spearheaded by Eric Gill and Jacob Epstein that would climax in the anti-sculptural gestures of Gilbert & George and Damien Hirst.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Liz McIvor recounts the story of `canal mania', the period of activity that helped develop Britain's modern financial economy, now centred in London.

programme.title: Canal Walks with Julia Bradbury
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury travels along the country's network of canals and their accompanying towpath trails. Julia kicks off her tour with a visit to the Scottish Highlands. Against the backdrop of Ben Nevis, her walk starts near Fort William where she embarks on her eight-mile trip along the Caledonian Canal, which cuts through beautiful mountain country.

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: Professor Robert Bartlett explores how the Normans developed from a band of marauding Vikings into the formidable warriors who conquered England in 1066. He tells how the Normans established their new province of Normandy - `land of the northmen' - in northern France. They went on to build some of the finest churches in Europe and turned into an unstoppable force of Christian knights and warriors.

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: This was the last of many hauntingly beautiful sketches and paintings Constable made of Salisbury Cathedral. He worked on it for years. During a bout of rheumatic fever, he propped the picture up against the foot of his bed. In the end, he was satisfied... 'At last,' he wrote, 'I have got the Great Salisbury into the condition I wish to see it.'
